title: Grateful Dead Live at Southern Star Amphitheater on 1985-08-30
lineage: Master Audience Cassettes> Nakamichi Dragon> Kind Kables RCA/XLR> Lunatec V3 (@ 24/96)> coax> Audiophile 2496> WaveLab 5.0> .wav @ 24/96>  Waves L3 UltraMaximizer > .wav @ 16/44.1 > TLH > FLAC16
source: MAC; (FOB) 2 x Sennheiser 441 > Sony D5 > Sony D5 > 2 x Maxell MX 90.  FOB, DFC, no more than 20 feet back from stage/ PAS - black shawl over mics (to avoid security).

ai_review.summary: Excellent fan‑taped recording that captures a blistering Drums > Space and solid jams, but Jerry’s vocal woes make the short 1985 show feel mixed.
ai_review.review: The mastering work by Alex Ford delivers crystal‑clear drums and space, which several reviewers call the best of ’85. Highlights include an explosive Drums > Space, a fiery Morning Dew, and strong performances of The Wheel, Bird Song and Scarlet > Touch. However, one reviewer notes Jerry Garcia’s voice sounded strained, giving the overall performance a mixed feel despite the superb audio.

ai_rating.rationale: Recording quality is rated excellent by most reviewers, while show quality is praised for jams but marred by vocal issues, yielding a solid overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Fans praise the crisp, well‑balanced sound and master work; drums and space are especially clear. No major dropouts or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A notably short 1985 set; tight pacing with a strong second‑set jam focus. Vocal fatigue is evident on some numbers, but the instrumental flow remains engaging.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His voice sounds strained and 'plug‑awful' due to heat, humidity and health issues.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are highlighted as outstanding—many call this the best ’85 Drums > Space ever.
